newsitem.title: QATAR: IMF forecasts rise in Qatar oil, gas exports.
newsitem.headline: IMF forecasts rise in Qatar oil, gas exports.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund has forecast that Qatar's oil and gas exports will more than double annual public sector income to $7 billion by the year 2000, the semi-official Qatar Economic Review said.
"There will be a 150 percent cumulative growth in public sector earnings reaching $7 billion by the year 2000," reported the review, quoting an IMF study.
In 1995, Qatar earned $2.4 billion from oil exports and around $800 million from other exports -- condensates, petrochemicals, fertilisers and steel.
The IMF said in coming years the income growth would mainly come from natural gas exports which would result in the "elimination of any fiscal deficit by the year 2000".
"By that time Qatar will once again become a capital surplus nation," the IMF study was quoted as saying.
Qatar's 120,000 citizens enjoy one of the world's highest per capita incomes of $22,000 per year, and until the early 1980s the state registered a cash surplus.

But massive investments in projects to develop the North Field -- the largest single reservoir of natural gas in the world -- and create new sources of revenue have caused balance of payment deficits in recent years. In 1995, the deficit reached $508 million.
The review said the IMF hoped the situation would change when Qatar started exporting gas from its first venture, the Qatar Liquefied Gas Company (Qatargas).
The first ship carrying 135,000 cubic metres of gas from Qatargas is scheduled to leave for Japan on December 24. Japan has agreed to buy six million tonnes a year for 25 years from January 1997.
Qatargas exports are projected to net $374 million in 1997, $522 million in 1998, increasing to $1.2 billion in 2001, the review said.

Qatar's second LNG project - Ras Laffan LNG Company, or Rasgas - which is expected to go on stream in July 1999, is projected to generate $105 million in the first year, rising to $665 million in 2001.
"Total revenue from LNG exports are expected to reach $1.9 billion over the next five years", the review said.
